rejected.statement: Eonatator was an extinct marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.
rejected.quote: Eonatator is an extinct genus of marine lizard belonging to the mosasaur family.

rejected.statement: Eonatator is a close relative of Halisaurus and belongs to the subfamily Halisaurinae.
rejected.quote: It is a close relative of Halisaurus, and part of the same subfamily, the Halisaurinae.

rejected.statement: Eonatator lived during the Late Cretaceous in North America, Colombia, and Sweden.
rejected.quote: It is known from the Late Cretaceous of North America, Colombia and Sweden.

rejected.statement: The type specimen of Eonatator sternbergii was approximately 2.6 meters long.
rejected.quote: Eonatator was a small mosasaur, with the type specimen of Eonatator sternbergii, UPI R 163, measuring approximately 2.6 m long.

rejected.statement: Eonatator coellensis is characterized by retracted nostrils located between the 7th and 17th maxillary teeth and a short rostrum.
rejected.quote: E. coellensis is diagnosed by more retracted nostrils, between the 7 and the 17 maxillary teeth, premaxilla and maxilla with a short rostrum anterior to the first teeth; presence of a septomaxilla, a large prefrontal that makes most of the margin of the outer nostril, a short and wide frontal, a parietal foramen located near of the fronto-parietal suture, a triangular surface of the parietal with two medial depressions and 22 caudal vertebrae.

rejected.statement: Remains of soft tissue and small vertebrae found under the pygal vertebrae of E. coellensis suggest the possibility that they belong to an embryo, though this is not fully confirmed.
rejected.quote: It have features of the mosasauroids, with three vertebrae with haemal arches and procoelic centra, that suggest the possibility that these small bones belong to an embryo of this species, although the lack of diagnostic fossils like the skull or teeth prevents a complete identification.

rejected.statement: The name Eonatator means "dawn swimmer", derived from Greek and Latin roots.
rejected.quote: The name Eonatator means "dawn swimmer" (Greek eos = dawn + Latin natator = swimmer).

rejected.statement: The species E. sternbergii was named in honor of Charles Hazelius Sternberg and his son Levi, who discovered the type specimen in 1918.
rejected.quote: The species is named in honour of Charles Hazelius Sternberg and his son, Levi, who discovered the type specimen in the Niobrara Chalk during the summer of 1918.

rejected.statement: The species E. coellensis was named after the town of Coello in Colombia, near where it was discovered.
rejected.quote: A second species, E. coellensis, was named for the town of Coello in the Department of Tolima in Colombia, near of which it was discovered.

rejected.statement: In 2005, Nathalie Bardet and colleagues reclassified Halisaurus sternbergii into the new genus Eonatator and established the subfamily Halisaurinae.
rejected.quote: In 2005, Halisaurus sternbergii was reassigned to its own genus, Eonatator by Nathalie Bardet and colleagues along with the description of Halisaurus arambourgi and the creation of the subfamily Halisaurinae.

rejected.statement: Lindgren and Siverson suggested in 2005 that Eonatator is an invalid junior synonym of Halisaurus sternbergii, but this view was not accepted by other researchers.
rejected.quote: In the same year, Lindgren and Siverson suggested that Eonatator is an invalid junior synonym and should be classified as H. sternbergii, but this has found no acceptance in other researchers who used the genus name Eonatator instead.

rejected.statement: A 2023 study tentatively assigned Eonatator coellensis to the genus Halisaurus, suggesting it is more closely related to Halisaurus than to the type species of Eonatator.
rejected.quote: They suggested that Phosphorosaurus ponpetelegans and Eonatator coellensis were more closely related to the genus Halisaurus than the type species of their respective genera. They tentatively assigned both of these species to Halisaurus.

rejected.statement: Fossils of Eonatator have been found in Kansas, Alabama, Sweden, and Colombia, dating from the Santonian to the Campanian stages.
rejected.quote: Eonatator is known from the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Chalk Formation (Late Coniacian to Early Campanian) of Kansas, from the Eutaw Formation (Santonian) and Mooreville Chalk Formation (Selma Group; Santonian-Lower Campanian) of Alabama (United States), from the Kristianstad Basin of southern Sweden (late early Campanian), and the unit Nivel de Lutitas y Arenas (Campanian) of the Olini Group in La Mesa, Colombia.

rejected.statement: The genus Eonatator was originally included in the genus Halisaurus before being placed in its own separate genus.
rejected.quote: Originalmente, Eonatator se incluía dentro del género Halisaurus, pero fue colocado en su propio género.

rejected.statement: The name Eonatator means 'morning swimmer', derived from the Greek word for dawn and the Latin word for swimmer.
rejected.quote: El nombre de Eonatator significa 'nadador del amanecer' (del griego eos = amanecer y el latín natator = nadador).

rejected.statement: The type species E. sternbergii was named in honor of Charles H. Sternberg and his son Levi, who discovered the type specimen in the Niobrara Chalk during the summer of 1918.
rejected.quote: E. sternbergii, la cual fue nombrada en honor de Charles H. Sternberg y su hijo Levi, quienes descubrieron el espécimen tipo en la Caliza de Niobrara Chalk durante el verano de 1918.

rejected.statement: A second species, E. coellensis, was named in 2013 after the municipality of Coello in the Tolima department of Colombia, near where it was discovered.
rejected.quote: Una segunda especie, E. coellensis, fue nombrada en 2013 por el municipio de Coello en el departamento de Tolima en Colombia, cerca del cual fue descubierta.

rejected.statement: The discovery of E. coellensis was made by Professor Luis Enrique Calderón and his son Ricardo, who found the fossil embedded in a dry creek bed, sent a sample to the Colombian Geological Service for confirmation, and subsequently organized an expedition to recover and investigate the find.
rejected.quote: El descubrimiento se logró gracias a Luis Enrique Calderón, profesor de Girardot, y su hijo Ricardo, quienes descubrieron el fósil incrustado en el lecho de una quebrada seca, tras lo cual tomaron una pequeña muestra que enviaron al Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC), confirmando que se trataba de un fósil y de esta manera se organizó una expedición para recuperar e investigar el hallazgo

rejected.statement: Fossils of Eonatator are known from the Smooky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation in Kansas, the Eutaw Formation in Alabama, the Kristianstad Formation in southern Sweden, and the Lutite and Sandstone Level Unit in Colombia.
rejected.quote: Eonatator se conoce del Miembro Smooky Hill Chalk de la Formación Niobrara (Coniaciense superior-Campaniense inferior) de Kansas, de la formación de Eutaw (Santoniense) y de la Formación Mooreville Chalk (Campaniense-Santoniense inferior) de Alabama, de la Formación Kristianstad de Suecia meridional (Campaniano) y de la unidad Nivel de Lutitas y Arenas (Campaniano) de Colombia.

rejected.statement: In 2005, Nathalie Bardet and colleagues reassigned Halisaurus sternbergii to its own genus, Eonatator, along with the description of Halisaurus arambourgi and the creation of the subfamily Halisaurinae.
rejected.quote: En 2005, Halisaurus sternbergii fue reasignado a su propio género, Eonatator por Nathalie Bardet y colaboradores junto con la descripción de Halisaurus arambourgi y la creación de la subfamilia Halisaurinae.

rejected.statement: Eonatator was among the smallest mosasaurs, with an adult skeleton length of only 2.65 meters.
rejected.quote: Eonatator estaba entre los mosasaurios más pequeños. La longitud del esqueleto, que representa a un adulto, es solamente de 2.65 metros en longitud.

rejected.statement: Like many mosasaurs, Eonatator likely fed primarily on smaller fish and marine reptiles.
rejected.quote: Como muchos mosasaurios, se alimentaba probablemente sobre todo de peces y reptiles marinos más pequeños.

rejected.statement: Specimens of E. coellensis are notable for preserving soft tissue remains in the ear region, neck, and thoracic and abdominal areas.
rejected.quote: El espécimen de esta especie es además notable por tener restos de tejido blando en la región del oído, el cuello y las regiones torácica y abdominal.

rejected.statement: Beneath the pigal vertebrae and the seventeenth dorsal vertebra, there is a series of 20 very small vertebral centra and a flattened bone measuring 25 centimeters in total length.
rejected.quote: Bajo las vértebras pigales y la decimoséptima vértebra dorsal hay una serie de 20 centros de vértebras muy pequeños y un hueso aplanado, que en conjunto miden 25 centímetros de largo.

rejected.statement: These small bones possess mosasauroid traits, such as hemal arches and procyclic centra, suggesting they may belong to embryos of this species, although the lack of diagnostic fossils like skulls or teeth prevents certain identification.
rejected.quote: Estos poseen rasgos de los mosasauroides, con tres vértebras con arcos hemales y centros procélicos, que sugieren la posibilidad de que estos pequeños huesos pertenezcan a embriones de esta especie, si bien la carencia de fósiles diagnósticos como el cráneo o dientes impiden una identificación certera.

rejected.statement: In any case, the presence of these potential embryonic bones would be consistent with ovoviviparity previously reported in other mosasauroids such as Carsosaurus.
rejected.quote: En cualquier caso, esto sería consecuente con el ovoviviparismo anteriormente reportado en otros mosasauroides como Carsosaurus.

rejected.statement: A cladistic analysis of Halisaurinae has indicated that Eonatator is the sister taxon of Halisaurus and represents one of the most basal known taxa among mosasaurs.
rejected.quote: Un análisis cladístico de Halisaurinae ha indicado que Eonatator es el taxón hermano de Halisaurus y que representa uno de los taxones más basales conocidos entre los mosasáuridos.

rejected.statement: The type specimen, a nearly complete skeleton originally referred to the genus Clidastes by Wiman and later to Halisaurus by Russell, is now housed at the Paleontological Institute of the University of Uppsala in Sweden.
rejected.quote: El espécimen tipo (UPI R 163, Instituto Paleontológico de la Universidad de Uppsala, Uppsala, Suecia), un esqueleto casi completo, originalmente fue referido el género Clidastes por Wiman y luego a Halisaurus por Russell.

rejected.statement: Eonatator lived during the Santonian to Campanian stages, from 85.7 to 72.2 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The parent group of Eonatator is Halisaurini.
rejected.quote: Parent group: Halisaurini

rejected.statement: Eonatator belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
rejected.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

rejected.statement: Eonatator is classified within the class Reptilia.
rejected.quote: Class: Reptilia

rejected.statement: The type species of the genus Eonatator is Eonatator sternbergii.
rejected.quote: Type species: Eonatator sternbergii

rejected.statement: In a 2023 phylogenetic analysis, Shaker et al. tentatively assigned Eonatator coellensis to the genus Halisaurus, suggesting it was more closely related to Halisaurus than to the type species of its own genus.
rejected.quote: En su descripción en 2023 de una nueva especie de Halisaurus, H. hebae, Shaker et al. llevaron a cabo un análisis filogenético de los miembros de la subfamilia Halisaurinae. Ellos sugirieron que Phosphorosaurus ponpetelegans y Eonatator coellensis estaban más cercanamente relacionados con el género Halisaurus que a las especies tipo de sus respectivos géneros. Ellos asignaron de forma tentativa a estas especies a Halisaurus.
